text:
Berkly Catton is 20 and leading the Seattle offense, which is a sentence the Kraken hoped to write eventually, not in November of his second season. He has 18 points in 22 games, up from 0.26 a game last season, plus his first NHL hat trick against Vancouver on Nov. 19. Daily Faceoff wondered whether he "might be the game-breaking talent the Kraken need."

The role change is real. He's playing 15:25 a night, up from 12:56, and he's on the ice for 37% of Seattle's power-play time, up from 15%. He's also one of the fastest skaters in the league (96th percentile for top speed and for bursts over 20 mph), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots coming off the rush last season.

The finishing won't hold. He has 8 goals on 3.8 expected, shooting 27%, and the Kraken have scored 8.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. His own chances in the last ten games are below his usual rate.

So: a breakout in role, a heater in results. The role is the part worth keeping an eye on.
headline: Berkly Catton has arrived, ahead of schedule
